images.title: A triangle is half its rectangle
images.purpose: Shows the altitude from X splitting the rectangle into two parts, each cut in half by the triangle.
images.composition: One rectangle, large and centred, with the triangle XDC inside it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A rectangle 5 units wide and 4 units tall, outlined dark. Bottom left corner D, bottom right corner C. X is a point on the top side, 2 units from the top left corner (so 3 units from the top right corner). Triangle XDC (lines X to D and X to C) is filled teal (#0072B2). The two leftover corner triangles of the rectangle, left one with legs 2 and 4 and right one with legs 3 and 4, are filled amber (#E69F00). A grey (#6B7280) dashed vertical line from X straight down to the point Y on DC, 2 units from D, with a small right angle mark at Y. It splits the rectangle into a 2 by 4 part and a 3 by 4 part; in each part the teal piece and the amber piece are the two halves. Labels: D, C, X, Y at those points; 5 cm under DC; 4 cm beside the right side; 10 cm² inside the teal triangle. Check: 1/2 × 5 × 4 = 10.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Teal and amber match in each part, so the triangle is half the rectangle wherever X sits.
images.description: Shows the altitude from X splitting the rectangle into two parts, each cut in half by the triangle.
images.context: Matches the worked example: DC = 5 cm, height 4 cm, area 10 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Have the child slide X along the top in imagination: the split always gives halves.

image_decisions.why: The altitude argument is visual: the matching halves on each side of XY carry the proof.
